claims: Sharia law is a comprehensive body of religious, moral, and legal principles derived from the Quran and Hadith.
Sharia law acts as a "path" for Muslim life.
Sharia law governs daily life, including prayers, fasting, business, and family issues.
Interpretation of Sharia law varies widely across different schools of thought and jurisdictions.
Religion, life, intellect, lineage, and property.
Sharia law often permits polygamy for men, subject to conditions.
Sharia law focuses on regulations for marriage, divorce, and inheritance.
Certain strict interpretations of Sharia law include severe punishments (hudud) like amputation for theft or stoning for adultery.
Sharia is rarely applied as a full legal code in modern states.
Sharia is mostly restricted to family law in many Muslim-majority countries.
Fiqh is human, changing interpretation of the law.
